summary: The prepared_gaia system defines a structurally interesting async multi-agent architecture inspired by GAIA methodology, with clear role separation across coordinator, workers, rooms, animal assistants, adoption agents, and applicants. However, every single inter-agent message send is commented out ('# In a real system, we would send this to coordinator'), CoordinatorAgent.assign_tasks() is an empty pass, and run_simulation.py never calls MultiAgentSystem.run_simulation() — so no agent ever starts or communicates. The system produces only print statements and no actual coordination. Beyond the non-functional communication layer, 5 of 13 requirements are entirely absent, including vaccination scheduling, staff registry, task prioritization, fair rotation, and emergency handling.

findings.description: All inter-agent message sends are commented out in every agent file. Agents print that they would send a message but never do. BaseAgent.send_message() and broadcast_message() are empty stubs with no implementation. No agent-to-agent communication occurs at runtime.
findings.evidence: reception_agent.py:48: '# await self.send_message("coordinator", registration_message)'; animal_assistant_agent.py:62: '# await self.send_message("coordinator", feed_request)'; room_agent.py:46: '# await self.send_message("coordinator", clean_request)'; adoption_agent.py:59: '# await self.send_message("coordinator", confirmation_message)'; applicant_agent.py:54: '# await self.send_message("coordinator", application)'

findings.description: CoordinatorAgent.assign_tasks() — the central coordination loop called every 2 seconds — is an empty method containing only 'pass'. No task scheduling, priority management, or worker matching is ever performed by the coordinator.
findings.evidence: coordinator_agent.py:66-68: async def assign_tasks(self): # Assign tasks based on availability and needs; pass

findings.description: run_simulation.py creates a MultiAgentSystem instance but never calls mas.run_simulation(). It just awaits asyncio.sleep(30) and exits. No agent ever calls start(), so no agent loops execute during the demo.
findings.evidence: run_simulation.py:25-30: mas = MultiAgentSystem(); await asyncio.sleep(30) — MultiAgentSystem.run_simulation() is never invoked

findings.description: No vaccination calendar, scheduling, or automated window monitoring is implemented anywhere in the system. No VaccinationSchedule model, no CalendarAgent equivalent, and no vaccination message types exist.
findings.evidence: service_layer.py TaskType enum: CLEAN, FEED, WALK, VACCINATION, INITIAL_CHECKUP, HEALTH, ADOPTION — VACCINATION type exists but no scheduling or window-monitoring agent or logic is implemented

findings.description: No staff registry or staff management exists. WorkerAgent has a hardcoded role 'caretaker' with no registration interface, no competency tracking, no preference management, and no limit enforcement.
findings.evidence: worker_agent.py:9-14: self.role = 'caretaker' # Default role; availability dict is hardcoded with no management API or registration protocol

findings.description: No task prioritization mechanism exists. Task entries in task_queue contain only task_id, type, entity_id, and worker_id with no priority field. There is no distinction between critical and routine tasks anywhere in the system.
findings.evidence: coordinator_agent.py:78-84: task_queue entries are plain dicts with task_id, type, room_id/animal_id, worker_id — no priority key; no PriorityAgent or equivalent class

findings.description: No fair rotation mechanism exists. CoordinatorAgent.find_available_worker() returns the first available worker of the required role without any workload tracking, task distribution history, or rotation logic.
findings.evidence: coordinator_agent.py:230-235: iterates worker_availability and returns first matching worker; no task-count tracking or distribution enforcement anywhere

findings.description: No emergency handling or schedule reconfiguration exists. There are no emergency event message types in the coordinator's dispatch, no EmergencyAgent, and no mechanism for handling staff unavailability or urgent animal admissions.
findings.evidence: coordinator_agent.py:26-60: handle_message switch covers newCleanRequest, newFeedRequest, newWalkRequest, newHealthRequest, newAnimalRegistration, newAdoptionApplication, and Confirm* types — no emergency types whatsoever

findings.description: CoordinatorAgent.is_task_assigned() checks task.get(task_type + '_id') but tasks store entity IDs under 'animal_id' and 'room_id', not 'feed_id' or 'clean_id'. This method always returns False, allowing unlimited duplicate task assignment.
findings.evidence: coordinator_agent.py:237-242: task.get(task_type + '_id') — for task_type='feed' looks for key 'feed_id'; but handle_feed_request at line 96 stores the entity as 'animal_id'

findings.description: Optional is used as a return type annotation in coordinator_agent.py but is not imported from typing, causing NameError at function definition time in Python 3.9 and earlier.
findings.evidence: coordinator_agent.py:1: from typing import Dict, Any, List — no Optional imported; line 231: def find_available_worker(self, role: str) -> Optional[str]

findings.description: Hardcoded timestamp strings '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z' appear in service_layer.py and multiple agent files instead of actual current timestamps, preventing any meaningful time-based audit trail or scheduling logic.

The async architecture with typed Enums (TaskType, TaskStatus, WorkerRole, AnimalState, RoomState), ServiceLayer, and clean abstract BaseAgent interface provides a well-structured foundation that would support a complete implementation with moderate development effort.
findings.evidence: service_layer.py:7-44: TaskType, TaskStatus, WorkerRole, AnimalState, RoomState enums; base_agent.py:1-35: clean async abstract interface with state management

missing_requirements: Rejestr pracowników i ról (Req 2) — no staff registry or management; WorkerAgent role is hardcoded with no registration API
Kalendarz szczepień (Req 7) — no vaccination calendar, scheduling, or window monitoring in any agent or service
Priorytetyzacja zadań (Req 10) — no priority system; tasks have no priority field and no critical vs routine distinction
Sprawiedliwa rotacja opieki (Req 11) — no rotation mechanism; coordinator uses first-match worker selection only
Obsługa nagłych zdarzeń (Req 12) — no emergency handling, no reconfiguration logic, no emergency message types in any agent
logical_inconsistencies: All inter-agent communication is commented out, making the multi-agent architecture non-functional — agents operate in complete isolation
CoordinatorAgent.assign_tasks() is empty, so the central coordination loop runs every 2 seconds but does nothing
run_simulation.py never calls MultiAgentSystem.run_simulation(), so agents never start their loops during the demo
is_task_assigned() checks wrong dictionary keys, always returning False and allowing unlimited duplicate task assignment
implementation_risks: Commented-out message sends mean no actual agent coordination occurs; the system is a collection of isolated objects that print status messages only
Empty assign_tasks() means the coordinator never proactively schedules any work
Duplicate task assignment guaranteed due to broken is_task_assigned() key lookup
NameError from Optional not imported in coordinator_agent.py on Python 3.9 and earlier
run_simulation.py demo creates agents but never runs them, giving a false impression of a working system
